strings.name: Robert Langer
strings.role: Chemical engineer, biomaterials researcher and MIT professor
strings.summary: Langer applies chemical engineering to drug delivery, biomaterials and tissue engineering, using polymers and nanoscale carriers to control therapeutic release. At MIT he trains interdisciplinary teams and supports translation through licensing and company formation; he is a Moderna co-founder.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through 16 November 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: He advanced drug delivery and biomaterials engineering, connecting laboratory innovation with medical devices and biotechnology companies.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: B.S. in chemical engineering, Cornell, 1970; Sc.D. in chemical engineering, MIT, 1974.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Giving materials therapeutic functions
strings.highlights.h1.text: Early work with Judah Folkman explored sustained release of large molecules; later biodegradable materials supported drug delivery and local treatments.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Connecting laboratories and industry
strings.highlights.h2.text: With collaborators, he developed tissue engineering and delivery systems and pursued translation through partnerships, patents and startups; approved products also required clinical, regulatory and industrial teams.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Named Welch Award recipient
strings.timeline.t1.text: The foundation recognized research on controlled release of therapeutic macromolecules and tissue-engineering materials, extending his work between chemistry and medicine.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Receiving the Kavli Prize in Nanoscience
strings.timeline.t2.text: His biomedical nanomaterials and drug-delivery research received recognition in the 2024 Kavli Prize.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Receiving the Queen Elizabeth Prize for Engineering
strings.timeline.t3.text: He was honored for advances and leadership linking engineering, chemistry and medicine, particularly controlled drug delivery.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Co-founding Moderna
strings.timeline.t4.text: He helped establish a company pursuing messenger RNA medicines, working with scientific and investment partners on its platform.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Approval for local polymer treatment
strings.timeline.t5.text: A local brain-cancer chemotherapy polymer technology developed with collaborators gained FDA approval, demonstrating translation of materials-based delivery.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Publishing Tissue engineering
strings.timeline.t6.text: With Joseph Vacanti, he published the Science article describing tissue repair through cells, materials and engineering.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Publishing sustained macromolecule release research
strings.timeline.t7.text: With Folkman, he reported polymer release of proteins and other large molecules in Nature, challenging prevailing doubts about delivery materials.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Doctorate and a move into medical research
strings.timeline.t8.text: After his MIT chemical engineering doctorate, he undertook postdoctoral work in Folkman’s surgical research laboratory on biomedical problems.
strings.timeline.t9.title: Completing Cornell studies
strings.timeline.t9.text: His chemical engineering bachelor’s degree preceded MIT graduate study and laid foundations for work spanning engineering and medicine.
